PullRequest.Title: agentHost: reconcile Copilot Connectors in place
PullRequest.Body:

Implements **item 1 only** of #341471. Follows #341470, which is now merged; this branch is based on current `main` and does not include a duplicate prerequisite commit.

## Summary

- Reconcile Connector membership/catalog changes in the existing SDK session instead of marking the session for destruction/resume. Share the launch-time reconciliation helper and resolve each session's own opaque account handle.
- Route an optional Connector name through the local management bridge. Use `forceConnectorName` only for a named reconnect and only when the runtime advertises `targetedReconcile`; ordinary refreshes do not force-restart Connectors.
- Coalesce per-chat refresh requests, defer active turns/background subagents, retain changes arriving during launch or an in-flight refresh, and keep failed requests available for retry.
- Refresh customization enablement, published MCP inventory/status/display names, and tool-list notifications after reconciliation. Preserve ordering with concurrent MCP Start/Stop.
- Add provider/session/service regressions and a bundled-runtime test using isolated local catalog and HTTPS MCP fixtures. Update the related architecture documentation.

No generated AHP contracts, authentication-recovery UI, general dispatch/history architecture, or items 2–4 are changed. The SDK version is inherited from `main` (`1.0.22-preview.0`), not changed by this PR.

## Safety limitation

The runtime can restart a stopped Connector when forced or when its configuration changes. This implementation deliberately defers live reconciliation if an affected Connector runtime server is stopped, not configured, or disabled, retaining the pending request and logging the reason. Generic refresh can therefore remain pending while any projected Connector is in those states. A named reconnect can still proceed when only unrelated Connectors are stopped. It does not convert Stop into Disable or recreate the session as a workaround.

The runtime test verifies actual RPC effects, tool inventory, membership removal/addition, targeted replacement, unrelated server initialization counts, and stopped-server deferral. It uses a temporary provider home, synthetic credentials, local services, and short-lived TLS certificates generated with OpenSSL on `PATH`; it does not use a real Connector account or send a model request.

**Still required before merge:** focused Azure pipeline 111 validation on Windows, Linux, and macOS x64, with two clean executions per platform for this lifecycle-sensitive test. No live Connector/UI smoke test or full test suite has been run. This PR is a draft pending that validation.

## Manual check

In a development Agents window with Connectors enabled, initialize a Copilot chat with two connected Connectors and an ordinary MCP server. Disconnect and reconnect one Connector while retaining the same chat. Its published tools/status/display name should update without an SDK destroy/resume, while the other Connector and ordinary MCP server remain undisturbed. Repeat during a turn/background subagent to verify deferral until idle. Stop a Connector server and verify a generic refresh leaves it stopped and logs the deferral instead of restarting it.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call path and persistence are explicit: tests assert stopped/unsupported requests remain pending, the send path awaits refreshConnectors whenever that bit is set, and every turn completion schedules it again. Exact IPC duration varies, but the repeated critical-path work is not speculative.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Sequential SDK/subprocess RPC calls and repeated MCP inventory/configuration work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: While a request remains deferred, cost grows with chat turns: each turn can trigger one post-turn attempt and the next send performs another awaited attempt; the same pattern occurs independently for every affected live session.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated pre-send latency and ongoing IPC/CPU load, with a slow attempt able to delay a prompt until the 60-second reconciliation timeout.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: A Connector change set the existing MCP launch-configuration refresh flag; the next operation replaced/resumed the session once, and the replacement did not retain an unreconcilable request to retry on every later turn.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new send path synchronously awaits a retained Connector request, while turn completion also schedules pending requests. Requests are deleted only after result.reconciled is true, so intentional stopped/not-configured/disabled state and permanently unsupported capabilities keep the request pending indefinitely.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added await at line 5595 puts refreshConnectors on every send/resume/start preparation path whenever hasPendingConnectorRefresh remains true. The same diff adds scheduling from _onChatTurnEnded, and _doRefreshConnectors only deletes the pending map entry when result.reconciled is true.
Findings.Title: Avoid retrying deferred Connector reconciliation on every turn
Findings.Impact: After an ordinary catalog refresh, a user who intentionally stopped/disabled a Connector—or whose runtime lacks the capability—pays repeated Agent Host/SDK RPCs before each subsequent prompt and again when turns end, even though no relevant state changed.
Findings.Evidence: For a stopped Connector, one attempt calls mcp.listConfigured before reconciliation, connectors.getCapabilities/getAccount/getStatus, mcp.listConfigured again, then the inventory refresh calls mcp.listConfigured once more; reconcileCopilotConnectors returns reconciled:false and the map entry is retained. Unsupported capability/account cases likewise retain the entry after several RPCs. The added tests explicitly expect pending:true for disabled/unavailable/unsupported/missing-account and stopped-server scenarios, and also verify that the send path retries a pending request before sending.
Findings.Recommendation: Retain the request without making it a per-turn retry condition: record the deferral reason and retry stopped-state requests on MCP status/configuration changes or an explicit refresh, retry capability/account negatives when the runtime/session/account changes, and back off transient failures. The send path should await only a newly actionable reconciliation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold or explicit Connector catalog refresh from the MCP/Customization UI
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A cold/explicit catalog read performs the Connector HTTP query; when connected membership or configuration changed, refresh() then awaits the local Agent Host management call and all idle live-session reconciliations before its promise completes. The onDidChange event can update existing views before that await, but marketplace queries and action completion remain blocked on it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One query per cold or explicit refresh after refresh-generation cancellation; warm getConnectors calls within 60 seconds issue none.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same catalog query was already performed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before catalog parsing and any live-session refresh decision.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the local Agent Host Connector refresh bridge
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bridge call when the accepted catalog changes connected membership/configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The bridge existed, but provider work only queued per-session configuration-change markers rather than completing live reconciliation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by refresh and therefore by cold marketplace queries and explicit UI actions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read capabilities/account/status, reconcile Connectors, and republish MCP inventory through SDK RPC
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per effective pending key per idle live session: multiple sequential SDK RPCs, with all idle sessions allowed concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No live per-session SDK reconciliation ran from this bridge; sessions were marked for replacement/resume on later use.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by the management bridge for accepted catalog changes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One catalog query and one management bridge call per accepted refresh, followed by one reconciliation per idle live Copilot session; each reconciliation examines the session's effective configured MCP server set.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider refreshes and live sessions fan out with Promise.all. Each chat uses its own queue; each session admits one refresh promise and coalesces identical pending keys, while changes arriving during an attempt can require a following pass.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: getConnectors uses a 60-second warm cache, while explicit refresh bypasses it. Session requests are coalesced by Connector name/generation, but deferred negative states remain pending rather than becoming a separately invalidated negative cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the workbench await, provider Promise.all, per-chat queue, and sequential SDK RPC chain are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneously live chats and runtime/network latency vary. The fan-out is real, but ordinary refreshes only invoke it when connected configuration changes, so no separate finding was filed for the bounded accepted-refresh path.
Scenarios.Verdict: The intended live update introduces bounded fan-out on actual catalog changes. Coalescing and per-chat sequencing keep this from independently meeting the reporting threshold; persistent deferred states are covered by the submitted finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Sending or resuming a chat with a retained Connector request, including an intentionally stopped Connector or unsupported runtime
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Before returning the existing SDK session to send/resume/start preparation, _refreshSessionConfiguration synchronously awaits refreshConnectors. A deferred request therefore runs before the model request can start.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Call mcp.listConfigured, connectors.getCapabilities/getAccount/getStatus, and refresh MCP inventory
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A stopped-server attempt performs three MCP inventory RPCs plus three Connector RPCs; unsupported variants perform a subset. This recurs per turn while pending.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The next use consumed one MCP launch-configuration refresh by replacing/resuming the session; it did not repeatedly probe the same negative state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All calls are sequentially awaited before a prompt can proceed; the attempt is bounded by the new 60-second timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh the Connector catalog inside SDK reconcile when the request is actionable
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one reconcile call per pending key/pass; deferred stopped/unsupported cases return before this network-backed operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old next-use path recreated/resumed the session rather than invoking live reconcile on every pending retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: When reached, it is also awaited before send and can run until the reconciliation timeout.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost repeats with every affected chat turn and every affected live session for as long as the stopped/disabled/unsupported/account-negative condition persists; a turn end can schedule one attempt and the next send can await another.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Work is serialized by the chat queue and one in-session refresh promise. Different chats can retry concurrently. Same-name requests coalesce, but a non-reconciled key is never cleared.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Positive reconciliation deletes the matching generation. Stopped/not-configured/disabled, unavailable capability, unsupported account/target, and missing account all retain the same undifferentiated pending key, with no negative-cache invalidation signal or retry backoff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: production code and added tests explicitly retain these negative states, retry before send, and schedule pending work after turns.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Individual local RPC latency and the prevalence of intentionally stopped Connector servers are not measured. The repeat count and critical-path placement are certain, and a slow RPC can consume the full timeout.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work regression; one medium-severity finding was submitted.

Scenarios.Scenario: Explicit named reconnect from Connector details
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action authorizes/refreshes the catalog, then a Connector already shown as connected awaits a named Agent Host refresh. Each live idle session resolves its own account and requests targeted reconciliation before the action reports completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/authorize Connector catalog and possibly open consent flow
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial catalog query per reconnect action, plus polling only when connection is not yet established.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Connect already refreshed and polled the account-backed catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes before named reconciliation is requested.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send forceConnectorName through workbench-to-Agent Host and per-session SDK targeted reconcile
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One management call, then one targeted reconcile per idle live session after coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No targeted name was routed; sessions were only marked for a later broad configuration refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before the reconnect action completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One targeted key per user reconnect action across all live sessions; distinct names remain distinct, repeated same-name requests coalesce by generation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Live sessions reconcile concurrently, each under its own chat queue; one session processes pending names sequentially.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Catalog reads use the 60-second getConnectors cache only when called through getConnectors; connect invokes explicit refresh. Successful targeted reconciliation clears that name, while unsupported targeted capability retains it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the optional name is traced end-to-end and the integration test verifies unrelated servers are not reinitialized.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Live-session count varies, and the runtime's targeted replacement duration is not measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the fan-out is tied to an explicit reconnect, targets only one Connector in each session, and preserves unrelated runtime servers. Persistent unsupported-target retries are covered by the submitted finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: MCP Start or Stop overlapping Connector reconciliation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Start/Stop increments the per-session control count and, when reconciliation started first, awaits the active Connector refresh before issuing the MCP lifecycle RPC. A control already in flight prevents a new reconciliation from starting.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Await Connector SDK reconciliation, then invoke mcp.startServer or mcp.stopServer
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One lifecycle RPC per Start/Stop; no extra lifecycle fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Start/Stop only used the per-server lifecycle sequencer and did not wait for Connector reconciliation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A later control can wait for the current reconciliation, preserving final-state ordering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One wait and one lifecycle RPC per user control operation; operations are additionally sequenced per server name.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Connector reconciliation and MCP controls are mutually ordered within one SDK session, while per-server lifecycle sequencing remains in place. Other chats/sessions are independent.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. A Connector attempt is bounded by 60 seconds and pending work remains available after cancellation/deferral.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ordering and timeout are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Overlap frequency and reconcile duration are unknown; worst-case wait is bounded by the configured timeout.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the serialization is an intentional same-session ordering constraint needed to prevent reconciliation from undoing a later control, and realistic overlap evidence is insufficient for a separate performance regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Launching a Copilot SDK session with Connectors enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After session creation and sandbox/script setup, launch resolves Connector capabilities/account and reconciles before wrapping/registering the session.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sequence per Connector-enabled session launch, with one status fallback only after reconciliation failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The launcher already performed the same reconciliation sequence inline; this PR extracts and shares it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remains on session startup before registration.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One reconciliation sequence per launched SDK session; catalog/runtime server cardinality affects status-map allocation and runtime work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The launch sequence is serial within a session; independent session launches follow existing provider admission/queue behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cross-session account/status cache is used because account handles are session-owned. Display-name maps are built from the returned status and retained by the session runtime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: deleted launcher code and the shared helper have equivalent startup boundaries.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runtime reconciliation duration depends on account/catalog state, but the launch cost was pre-existing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression on launch; the helper refactor preserves the existing boundary count and map construction.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 17 changed files and complete diff pages. Traced catalog refresh, named reconnect, per-session live reconciliation, send/resume, turn completion, MCP lifecycle ordering, and launch-time reconciliation. Submitted one performance finding for persistent negative Connector states causing repeated critical-path SDK RPCs on every turn; no qualifying regression fix was recorded.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
